title: Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat after decades

needs.need: Who Mississippi's last Black senator and last Democratic senator were, and when they served.
needs.accepts: Names Blanche K. Bruce (served 1875 to 1881) as Mississippi's previous Black senator, credited to a named source; naming John Stennis (last elected 1982, served until 1989) as its previous Democratic senator is a plus but not required.

example.value: Blanche K. Bruce, Mississippi's previous Black senator, served from 1875 to 1881. Colom is the first Democrat to win a Mississippi Senate seat since John Stennis in 1982.
example.source: U.S. Senate Historical Office; Dawn for Stennis

needs.need: What the projected 55 Democratic seats already settle about Senate control, with Alaska still undecided.
needs.accepts: A credited statement that 55 of the Senate's 100 seats is a Democratic majority whatever Alaska's result. Adding that 55 falls short of the 60 votes needed to end a filibuster is a plus but not required.

example.value: With 55 of 100 seats, Democrats would control the Senate regardless of Alaska, though short of the 60 votes needed to invoke cloture on most legislation.
example.source: U.S. Senate, party division and Rule XXII

needs.need: How Hyde-Smith has responded to the projected defeat.
needs.inStory: Hyde-Smith, who had served since 2018, called Colom to concede.
needs.accepts: Reports Hyde-Smith's concession (a call to Colom or a public concession statement), credited to a named source.

example.value: Hyde-Smith called Colom to concede and then posted a concession speech online.
example.source: Cindy Hyde-Smith's concession video on X, as reported by Dawn

needs.need: When Colom is scheduled to begin his Senate service.
needs.inStory: Colom is scheduled to take office on January 3
needs.accepts: Gives January 3, 2027, as the start of Colom's term or of the incoming Senate, credited to a named source.

example.value: The incoming Senate term begins at noon on January 3, 2027.

needs.need: Whether Mississippi's flip was isolated or part of a broader set of Democratic Senate gains.
needs.accepts: The number of Republican-held Senate seats Democrats flipped in this election, including Mississippi (eight), credited to a named source; a final seat total alone does not meet it.

example.value: Democrats flipped eight Senate seats previously held by Republicans, including Mississippi.

needs.need: How large Mississippi's Black population is, to size what a 140-year gap in representation means.
needs.accepts: Mississippi's Black share of population (about 38%, the highest of any U.S. state), credited to a named source such as the U.S. Census Bureau.

example.value: About 38% of Mississippi residents are Black, the highest share of any state.

needs.need: What shifts in the vote produced Colom's upset in a state Republicans have held for decades.
needs.accepts: A credited count or specific account of counties that switched to Colom (not merely counties he won), with any preliminary status stated.

example.value: A preliminary analysis found that Colom flipped at least 18 counties.

notes: The story's "the full Senate balance remains unresolved" is loose: on the reported projections 55 seats is a majority whatever Alaska's result; senate-majority asks a card to say so. Bruce was chosen by the state legislature, before popular Senate elections; a card calling Colom the first Black senator elected by popular vote in Mississippi is right. Treat seat totals as projections.
